meta.title: Pacific Highway Kerb & Gutter — Rain & Telstra Hit
meta.summary: Rain delayed trench dewatering; unexpected Telstra conduit found at CH 480 halts work in 7 m section.

weather.impact: 4 am rain flooded trench; pumps ran all morning, ground workable by lunch

materials.name: Concrete
materials.notes: original 10 am moved to 13:00, not poured

issues.title: Telstra conduit strike
issues.details: Uncharted Telstra pit at CH 480; conduit 300 mm deep crossing alignment CH 478–485. Work stopped in 7 m zone.
issues.actionRequired: Telstra rep to attend; decide relocation or protection before resuming.

issues.title: Trench flooding
issues.details: Rain from 04:00 flooded trench; 2 pumps (3 & 4 inch) dewatered by lunch.

nextSteps: Await Telstra representative to resolve conduit conflict
Pour concrete for first 30 m kerb section if weather permits
Continue formwork and sub-base preparation around Telstra zone
Book compaction testing for next sub-base lengths

sections.title: Work Progress
sections.content:
**Kerb & gutter southbound CH 450–520**
- Traffic control: 2 lanes closed, 40 km/h zone, TCP approved.
- Trench excavated (CAT 320) but halted by water; pumps cleared by midday.
- Sub-base placed and compacted to 99% standard Proctor on first 30 m.
- Formwork complete and line-checked within tolerance; ready for concrete pour.

**CH 520–600**
- Surveyor pegged alignment; no excavation yet.

sections.title: Service Conflict
sections.content: At CH 480 excavation uncovered an uncharted Telstra pit and 300 mm deep conduit running diagonally across alignment CH 478–485. Dial-Before-You-Dig locator confirmed; work in 7 m window suspended. Project manager and client notified; awaiting Telstra rep to discuss relocation or protection measures, potentially 2-day delay.

sections.title: Plant & Equipment
sections.content:
- CAT 320 excavator: 3 h on trench
- Bomag padfoot roller: 2 h on sub-base compaction
- 3 & 4 inch pumps: all day dewatering
- Concrete truck rescheduled 10 am → 1 pm (not used)

systemPrompt:
You are a construction site report assistant. You convert numbered site notes from a construction site into a structured JSON report.

INPUT
- NOTES: numbered site notes captured on site. Each note is one input item — text, voice transcript, image, video, or document. Non-text items appear as numbered placeholders (e.g. "[image 1]", "[image 2]", "[video 1]", "[document 1]") at their position. You cannot see their contents, but you should acknowledge that the attachment exists.

OUTPUT
Return ONLY valid minified JSON in this exact shape:
  { "report": { "meta": {...}, "weather": ..., "workers": ..., "materials": [...], "issues": [...], "nextSteps": [...], "sections": [...] } }

- Always return the FULL report. Include every top-level field, even when empty.
- Use null for missing "weather" / "workers", [] for empty arrays, "" for missing strings.
- Do NOT wrap the JSON in markdown fences. Do NOT add prose before or after.

SCHEMA
"meta":          { "title": str, "reportType": "site_visit|daily|inspection|safety|incident|progress", "summary": str, "visitDate": "YYYY-MM-DD"|null }
"weather":       { "conditions", "temperature", "wind", "impact" }              (object or null)
"workers":       { "totalWorkers": num, "workerHours", "notes",
                   "roles": [{ "role", "count": num, "notes" }] }                (object or null)
"materials":     [{ "name", "quantity", "quantityUnit", "condition", "status", "notes" }]
"issues":        [{ "title", "category", "severity", "status", "details", "actionRequired" }]
"nextSteps":     [str]
"sections":      [{ "title", "content": "markdown" }]

RULES
- Populate "meta.title" with a short, human-readable title (e.g. "Site Visit — Wet Weather") and "meta.summary" with a one-sentence overview.
- Use sections to capture work progress, observations, and narrative detail. Materials list everything mentioned (concrete, steel, timber, pipes, etc.) — do NOT extract cost/price information; that's handled outside this flow.
- NEVER invent data not in the notes. Keep strings concise. Deduplicate facts.

EXAMPLE
{ "report": { "meta": { "title": "Site Visit — Wet Weather", "reportType": "daily", "summary": "Wet conditions delayed concrete pour", "visitDate": null }, "weather": { "conditions": "wet", "temperature": "20C", "wind": null, "impact": "Pour delayed by 1 hour" }, "workers": null, "materials": [{ "name": "Concrete", "quantity": "50", "quantityUnit": "m³", "condition": null, "status": "delivered", "notes": null }], "issues": [], "nextSteps": ["Order rebar"], "sections": [{ "title": "Foundation Work", "content": "Concrete pour started in zone A despite wet weather." }] } }
userPrompt:
NOTES:
[1] morning. so were on the pacific highway job today, doing the kerb and gutter on the southbound lane from chainage 450 to about 520
[2] traffic control is set up, looks good. two lanes closed, one open with a 40 zone. the TCP was approved last week
[3] weather is absolute rubbish today. been raining since like 4am. the trench is full of water
[4] pumps are running trying to get the water out of the trench. got 2 pumps going, 3 inch and a 4 inch
[5] the excavator operator Steve is on site. CAT 320, been using it to dig the kerb trench. but cant do much till the water is out
[6] surveyor is here pegging out the next section of kerb from chainage 520 to 600
[7] the string line is set up for the first 30 meters of kerb. form work going in now. Kevs crew is on it, 4 guys
[8] concrete truck is booked for 10am but honestly with this rain I dont know if we'll be ready. might have to push to after lunch
[9] called the batch plant, pushed the concrete to 1pm. they were sweet with it
[10] rain has eased off a bit. pumps have got the trench mostly dry. still muddy as hell but workable
[11] the stabilised sand delivery showed up early which is good. 2 truck and dogs, about 40 tonne total. dumped it on the stockpile area
[12] the roller is here too, bomag padfoot for compaction of the sub base. operator Dazza is ready when we need him
[13] laying the sub base material in the first section now. about 100mm depth, well compact it to 98% standard
[14] oh theres been a services issue. telstra pit at chainage 480 that wasnt on the plans. we've hit a conduit. stopping work in that area till we get a location done
[15] called dial before you dig, theyve got a locator coming out this afternoon. pain in the arse
[16] the rest of the kerb prep is going ahead though, just working around the telstra issue
[17] compaction testing on the first section. passed. 99% standard proctor. beauty
[18] lunch. weathers cleared up properly now, even some sun. ground is drying out
[19] locator arrived, confirm there's a telstra conduit running diagonally across our alignment at chainage 478 to 485. its only 300mm deep too. way too shallow
[20] gonna have to get a telstra rep out to discuss relocation or protection. this could delay us a couple days in that section. not ideal
[21] emailed the project manager and the client about the telstra issue. sent photos and the locator report
[22] managed to get the formwork done on the first 30m section despite the dramas. ready for concrete tomorrow if the weather holds
[23] kerb forms look good. Kev checked the string line, everything is within tolerance. grade is spot on
[24] end of day. packed up the traffic control for the night shift to set up their layout. theyre doing line marking on the northbound lanes tonight
[25] total crew today was 8 plus traffic controllers. excavator for 3 hours, roller for 2 hours, 2 x pumps all day. got through it considering the weather and the telstra surprise
